target.title: fix(secrets): collect persona-level TTS provider SecretRefs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Persona-level TTS provider API keys were not collected as SecretRefs and agent persona registry paths bound the wrong path segment as providerId (literal `providers` instead of `elevenlabs`). That breaks secrets plan/audit and runtime resolution for agent persona TTS keys.

Fixes #89607

## Summary

The secret collector walks `messages.tts.providers.*.apiKey` but does not walk `messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` or `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`. When a persona overrides the TTS provider config with a file-source SecretRef, the secret resolver never sees the ref, so the `apiKey` reaches the plugin as an unresolved object instead of the actual key string. The plugin then reports `not configured`.

This fix:
- Adds persona-level provider iteration in `collectTtsApiKeyAssignments`
- Registers two new target paths in the secret target registry (`messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` and `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`)
- Extends `hasAgentRuntimeSecretRefs` to detect persona-level TTS refs
- Adds 5 regression tests covering top-level, persona-level, combined, empty-persona, and agent-level persona paths

Closes #89607

## Evidence

Terminal output from `tsx` against the patched branch showing correct `providerId` binding and persona file SecretRef collection (see Real behavior proof for full capture).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Agent persona TTS SecretRef paths must resolve `providerId` to the provider key (e.g. `elevenlabs`), not the literal `providers` segment, so plan/audit/runtime metadata match the configured provider. Persona-level file SecretRefs must be collected under `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64, Node v22, OpenClaw branch `fix/tts-persona-secretref` at `/tmp/oc-89636`, commit after providerId index fix.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  ```bash
  cd /tmp/oc-89636
  pnpm exec vitest run src/secrets/target-registry.test.ts src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts
  pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-tts-providerid.mjs
  pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-tts-collect.mjs
  ```

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched source:

  ```console
  ✓ src/secrets/target-registry.test.ts (10 tests)
  ✓ src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts (5 tests)
  Test Files  2 passed (2)
  Tests  15 passed (15)

  $ pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-tts-providerid.mjs
  {"path":"agents.list.0.tts.personas.narrator.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey","entryId":"agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey","providerId":"elevenlabs"}
  {"path":"agents.list.0.tts.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey","entryId":"agents.list[].tts.providers.*.apiKey","providerId":"elevenlabs"}
  {"path":"messages.tts.personas.narrator.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey","entryId":"messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey","providerId":"elevenlabs"}
  {"path":"messages.tts.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey","entryId":"messages.tts.providers.*.apiKey","providerId":"elevenlabs"}

  $ pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-tts-collect.mjs
  assignments:
  {"path":"agents.list.0.tts.personas.narrator.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey","ref":{"source":"file","provider":"default","id":"/tmp/redacted-narrator-key.txt"}}
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Registry resolution returns `providerId: "elevenlabs"` for agent persona TTS paths (index 7). Collector emits the persona file SecretRef under the agent TTS path prefix.
- **What was not tested:** Live OpenClaw gateway TTS synthesis against a real ElevenLabs account using the resolved persona SecretRef (no provider credentials in this environment). Optional fail-open degradation for missing TTS SecretRefs remains tracked in openclaw/openclaw#101204.


## Rank-up follow-up (2026-07-09)

ClawSweeper P1: include global persona TTS refs in agent-runtime targets.

- Added `messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` to `STATIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_BASE_TARGET_IDS`
- Extended the agent-runtime target coverage assertion to require both global and agent-level persona paths

Terminal confirmation on branch head:

```console
$ node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/cli/command-secret-targets.test.ts -t "persona TTS targets in the agent runtime"
 ✓ command secret target ids > includes persona TTS targets in the agent runtime command target set

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 39 skipped (40)
```

Still not tested: live `openclaw infer tts convert` with a file-source persona SecretRef (no TTS provider credentials in this environment).

target.title: feat(durable): hand off wakes to session queue
target.body:
# PR5/5 - internal session delivery handoff + final hardening

## What Problem This Solves

This finishes the beta3 durable-core stack by turning resolved durable wake
obligations into an internal session delivery-queue handoff on gateway startup.
After PR4 made wakes inspectable and controllable, PR5 gives the durable runtime
a concrete recovery path: a resolved wake is replayed, persisted with delivery
evidence, and queued for the owning OpenClaw session without inventing external
channel sends.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR5/5
- Clean PR5 comparison: `a30e2b6ce4e5f1390599380aedc82078c98854f7..443ffd2292e146fad3c089a03382a5f4702632f7`
- PR4 dependency: `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105844`
- GitHub base rationale: existing PR1-PR4 stack PRs target `release/2026.7.1`; the PR4 branch exists on the fork, not as an upstream base branch, so this PR follows stack convention while documenting the exact PR4-head diff.

## Scope

- Adds `createDurableWakeSessionDeliveryHook`, which resolves durable wakes to
  agent/session keys and enqueues one internal `systemEvent` via the session
  delivery queue.
- Wires gateway startup durable wake replay through that hook.
- Persists delivery evidence with `internalDelivery: "session_delivery_queue"`
  and `noExternalSend: true`.
- Extends focused replay/startup tests for idempotency, startup replay, ambiguous
  target handling, and no autonomous resume/abandon/create-new policy.
- Updates durable docs to clarify the `delivered` state and CLI wake-attempt
  evidence.

## Non-scope

- No Discord, Signal, Slack, plugin, or other external transport delivery is
  implemented or claimed.
- No cron mutation.
- No release/changelog/package churn from the stale old PR5 ancestry.
- No broad durable orchestration policy changes beyond this internal handoff.

## Evidence

Clean scope:

```text
6 files changed, 372 insertions(+), 50 deletions(-)
```

Focused behavior:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/durable/wake-delivery-replay.test.ts src/durable/startup.test.ts
# pass: 2 files, 14 tests
```

Adjacent durable CLI/Gateway/read-path proof:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/durable.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/durable.test.ts src/durable/wake-controls-inspection.test.ts
# pass: 3 Vitest shards, 4 files, 25 tests
```

Static/docs gates:

```bash
pnpm check:test-types
# pass

pnpm check:docs
# pass

git diff --check a30e2b6ce4e5f1390599380aedc82078c98854f7..HEAD
# pass
```

Remote proof attempts were made but unavailable in this shell:

```text
blacksmith-testbox: blocked, blacksmith CLI not found in PATH
aws Crabbox: blocked, broker login missing
```

## Upgrade contract

This PR adds no schema migration. It writes wake delivery attempts using the
existing durable wake attempt ledger and queues internal session deliveries using
the existing session delivery queue idempotency contract. Repeated startup replay
must not duplicate queued events once a wake is marked delivered.

## Risk / limits

- Main risk is semantic: reviewers should confirm `delivered` remains scoped to
  internal durable/session handoff and cannot be mistaken for external channel
  transport success.
- Remote Testbox proof is still desirable before merge because local provider
  setup blocked it here.
- Full release validation was not run for this narrow PR5 slice.

@clawsweeper review



### Live Gateway startup/restart proof at PR5 head

Additional live Gateway startup/restart proof at PR5 head `443ffd2292e146fad3c089a03382a5f4702632f7` was collected using a real local Gateway process twice against the same isolated state dir.

This proof intentionally disables external channels/plugins and does not claim Discord, Slack, Telegram, plugin, or other external transport delivery, end-user-visible consumption, live attached-session consumption, topology cleanup, or merge readiness. In PR5, `delivered` means internal durable/session-queue handoff only: ownership transferred to the persisted session delivery queue.

Result summary:

```text

- one resolved wake moved pending -> delivered

Representative startup logs:

Reset-boundary proof remains scoped to the existing focused test: queued `agentTurn` entries carry `expectedSessionId` and are skipped across a session-generation mismatch, while PR5 durable wake handoff queues a `systemEvent` against the canonical current session key. This surfaces the durable wake internally without autonomous resume or new-session policy.

target.title: fix(recovery): reclaim terminal-phase reply operations in stuck-session recovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Stuck-session recovery unconditionally keeps the lane for any reply operation in the registry (`reason=active_reply_work`), even operations that will never produce progress — permanently wedging the lane until gateway restart.
- **Problem**: Two phantom scenarios exist:
  1. A ReplyOperation with terminal phase (completed/failed/aborted) remains in the registry via `retainFailureUntilComplete` or `terminalSettleTimer`. Recovery sees `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive = true` and keeps the lane forever — no progress data means `isActiveRunProgressStale` never triggers.
  2. A ReplyOperation in non-terminal phase (running) but with zero diagnostic progress events (`lastProgressAgeMs = undefined`). `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` for undefined ages, so the stale-progress path never fires. The lane stays wedged.
- **Solution**: 
  1. Terminal-phase check before `active_reply_work`/`keep_lane` — reclaim completed/failed/aborted operations after the 60s terminal settle window.
  2. `fallbackAgeMs` parameter in `isActiveRunProgressStale` — when no diagnostic progress exists, fall back to the overall session age so phantoms without any activity can still be reclaimed.
- **What changed**: `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts` (terminal-phase branch + `fallbackAgeMs` in stale check), `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` (settle window guard test, no-progress phantom test, `it.each` for all three terminal phases)
- **What did NOT change**: `reply-run-registry.ts`, `runs.ts`, `classifySessionAttention`, `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible`; deferred-maintenance and running-phase behavior; embedded run handle detection

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #105712
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Issue #105712 reports that a chat session lane can get wedged by a phantom active run: the lane's claim says an `embedded_run` is doing reply work, but no such run exists. The stuck-session recovery detects the stuck session, but then declines to act because `reason=active_reply_work` exempts the claim unconditionally. The only recovery is a full gateway restart.

This affects builds where a ReplyOperation finishes but stays in the registry (terminal phase) or where a run died before emitting any diagnostic events (no-progress phantom). The root cause is twofold:
1. `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined`
2. The reply-work branch has no fallback for terminal-phase operations

The diagnostic classification system (`classifySessionAttention`) also cannot set `allowActiveAbort: true` for these phantoms because there's no active work kind.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Session recovery keeps the lane for terminal-phase or no-progress reply operations, permanently wedging the channel lane until gateway restart
- Real environment tested: Linux (Ubuntu Azure VM), Node v24.14.0, branch `fix/reclaim-terminal-embedded-run-105712`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Run tests that exercise the actual recovery function
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)

$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)

$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  115 passed (115)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Terminal-phase reply operations (completed/failed/aborted, age > 60s settle window) are reclaimed — logged as "reclaiming terminal reply operation"
  2. Terminal-phase operations still within the 60s settle window keep the lane — logged as "still within settle window"
  3. No-progress phantoms (phase=running, no diagnostic activity, session age > 5 min) are reclaimed via `fallbackAgeMs` — logged as "reclaiming stale active reply work"
  4. Running-phase and queued-phase operations with active diagnostic progress keep the lane (unchanged)
  5. Deferred-maintenance operations keep the lane (unchanged)
  6. The `allowActiveAbort: true` recovery path is unaffected

- What was not tested:
  - Full gateway E2E with real Slack channel and phantom injection (requires long-running gateway and specific race conditions to reproduce)
  - The `terminalSettleTimer` path (60s settle window) is respected by the settle guard — if the timer fires normally the operation auto-clears before recovery sees it
  - macOS/Windows platforms (Linux only)

**Test evidence (post-rebase, Node v22.19.0)**:

Runtime tests — all 5 new tests pass:
```console
 ✓ reclaims terminal-phase reply operations (phase=completed, phantom embedded_run) instead of keeping the lane
 ✓ reclaims terminal-phase reply operations (phase=failed, phantom embedded_run) instead of keeping the lane
 ✓ reclaims terminal-phase reply operations (phase=aborted, phantom embedded_run) instead of keeping the lane
 ✓ keeps the lane when terminal-phase reply operation is still within the settle window
 ✓ reclaims no-progress reply operations (phase=running, phantom without diagnostic activity)
 ✓ (25 more pre-existing tests pass)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed | 1 failed (31)
```
The single failure (`logs stopped cron context when aborting an active embedded run`) is a pre-existing SQLite version issue (Node 22.19.0 embeds SQLite 3.50.4; OpenClaw requires 22.22.3+) — unrelated to this PR.

**E2E reclaim proof** — real gateway components + real `diag.warn()` terminal output:

```console
=== failed (retainFailureUntilComplete) ===
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation: sessionId=e2e-failed sessionKey=agent:main:e2e-failed age=61s queueDepth=1 activeSessionId=e2e-failed-session phase=failed
stuck session recovery: sessionId=e2e-failed-session sessionKey=agent:main:e2e-failed age=61s action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true released=0
stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted action=abort_embedded_run ... aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false released=0
→ Queued message: drained

=== aborted (running → abortByUser) ===
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation: sessionId=e2e-aborted ... phase=aborted
stuck session recovery: ... action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true
stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted ... aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false
→ Queued message: drained

=== completed (setPhase, no complete()) ===
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation: sessionId=e2e-completed ... phase=completed
stuck session recovery: ... action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true
stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted ... aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false
→ Queued message: drained

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

The diagnostic warnings (`diag.warn()` calls inside `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession`) are captured directly and printed as terminal output — no mocks, no assertions-only. This is the exact log output that a running gateway produces when it reclaims a terminal-phase phantom.

**Additional real-runtime evidence**:
```
=== Gateway Dist Proof — Fix Code Verification ===
[1] recoverStuckDiagnosticSession loaded: OK ✓
[2] fallbackAgeMs in running dist: YES ✓
[3] terminalPhaseAgeMs in running dist: YES ✓
[4] Settle guard (6e4=60s): PRESENT ✓

=== Environment ===
Node: v22.22.2 (gateway process)
Branch: fix/reclaim-terminal-embedded-run-105712
Gateway health: {"ok":true,"status":"live"} (port 18789)

=== Test Results ===
runtime tests: 30/31 passed (1 pre-existing SQLite env failure)
integration tests: 10/10 passed (was 7)
Total: 40/41 passed across 2 suites
```

- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: No policy/permission surface touched
  - ✅ Enum completeness: All three terminal phases (`completed`/`failed`/`aborted`) covered via OR condition. No-diagnostic-progress phantom handled by `fallbackAgeMs` fallback (applies to any phase). Settle window (60s) prevents premature reclamation. `it.each` covers all three terminal phases + explicit settle window + no-progress tests.
  - ✅ Path coverage: Both call sites of `isActiveRunProgressStale` (active embedded run path and reply work path) pass `fallbackAgeMs`. The terminal-phase check is a new branch added before the existing `active_reply_work` return.
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: Both paths (terminal-phase reclaim and stale-progress reclaim) call the same `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` function with `forceClear: true`. `clearState()` in `expireStaleReplyRunBySessionId` is idempotent (guarded by `stateCleared`).

## Root Cause

Two separate gaps in `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts`:

1. **Terminal-phase gap**: The `!activeSessionId && activeWorkSessionId && isEmbeddedAgentRunActive(...)` branch unconditionally returns `keep_lane` for any ReplyOperation still in the registry, even terminal-phase operations that have already completed/failed/aborted.

2. **No-progress gap**: `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined` (no diagnostic events recorded). A phantom run that dies before first transcript flush leaves zero diagnostic activity, so the stale-progress path never fires. The session is permanently exempt from `keep_lane` → `active_reply_work`.

Both gaps interact: the diagnostic system sees no active work kind for these phantoms, so `classifySessionAttention` classifies them as `recoveryEligible` (correct) but `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible` sees no `embedded_run` and never sets `allowActiveAbort: true`. The maintenance recovery path hits the `active_reply_work` gate and returns `keep_lane` — permanently.

## Regression Test Plan

| Target file | Scenario | What it protects |
|-------------|----------|-----------------|
| `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` | phase=running + no handle → keep_lane | Active work not interrupted |
| (same) | phase=running + allowActiveAbort → abort | Stale abort path unchanged |
| (same) | phase=completed/failed/aborted + age > 60s → reclaim | **New**: Terminal zombies reclaimed |
| (same) | phase=completed + age < 60s settle window → keep_lane | **New**: Settle window respected |
| (same) | phase=running + no diagnostic activity + old session → reclaim | **New**: No-progress phantoms reclaimed |
| (same) | phase=deferred_maintenance → keep_lane | Deferred maintenance preserved |
| `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts` | Full recovery flow | Recovery coordinator integration |
| `reply-run-registry.test.ts` | All registry operations | Registry lifecycle unaffected |

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None (fix to internal session recovery logic)

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: Unit tests for all three terminal phases + settle window guard + no-progress phantom + running + deferred-maintenance + stale-abort paths. 152 tests total across 4 suites.
- Edge cases checked: Non-terminal phases not reclaimed; settle window (< 60s) prevents premature reclaim; `undefined` phase handled safely by `else` fallthrough; empty diagnostic activity falls back to session age
- What you did NOT verify: Full gateway long-run with real phantom injection (requires production race conditions); macOS/Windows platforms (Linux only)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only changes behavior for terminal-phase operations and no-progress phantoms that were previously incorrectly kept alive
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The fix addresses both identified phantom scenarios (terminal-phase and no-progress) at the recovery decision point with minimal code change (one new `if` branch + `fallbackAgeMs` parameter). ClawSweeper's two P1 findings (phase-less phantom handling and terminal settlement guard) are both addressed.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: (1) Checking `isReplyRunEvidenceStale` in the recovery runtime — rejected because the recovery function doesn't directly access the operation object. (2) Narrowing `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive` in `runs.ts` — rejected because of broader usage across message queueing and abort paths. (3) Adding fallback to `classifySessionAttention` — rejected because the classification layer should stay focused on diagnostic activity, not reply-run-registry state.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Premature reclamation during the 60s terminal settle window, allowing follow-up turns to interleave with still-draining terminal delivery.

**Mitigation**: The settle guard checks `terminalPhaseAgeMs >= 60s` before reclaiming. In practice `stuckSessionWarnMs` (180s default) >> 60s settle window, so by the time recovery fires, the settle timer has long expired. The guard adds defense-in-depth for lower warn thresholds.

**Additional risk**: No-progress phantoms with `queueDepth = 0` (no queued messages) are still not reclaimed because `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when there's no work to process. This is by design — if no messages are queued, there's nothing to recover. Once a new message arrives, `queueDepth` becomes > 0 and recovery can proceed.

**Compatibility impact**: None.

Related to #105712

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Tlon Urbit SSE `openStream` armed a 60s connect `setTimeout` and only cleared it after a successful `urbitFetch`. When the connect fetch rejected (DNS/SSRF/network) or returned non-OK, the timer stayed armed until it fired, and reconnect storms could stack dangling timers in the Gateway process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap the connect fetch in `try/finally` and always `clearTimeout`, matching the zalouser probe timeout cleanup pattern, so failed connects release the timer immediately without changing the connect deadline or stream lifecycle.

## User Impact

Flaky Urbit hosts no longer leave dangling connect timers in long-running Tlon monitors during reconnect failures.

## Evidence

### Unit regression (mocked fetch + fake timers)

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.test.ts --reporter=verbose

The reject case uses a closed loopback port (`127.0.0.1:9`) so the production transport fails before headers.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Failed SSE connect attempts no longer leave uncleared 60s AbortController timers, including under repeated failure.
- **Canonical reachability path:** Tlon monitor reconnect → `UrbitSSEClient.openStream` → production `urbitFetch` / `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → reject or non-OK → `finally { clearTimeout(timeoutId) }`.

target.title: fix(mattermost): bound websocket handshake waits at 30s

## What Problem This Solves

Mattermost's default websocket factory set `maxPayload` but not `handshakeTimeout`. `createMattermostConnectOnce` waits for the `open` event; when a peer accepts TCP but never completes the websocket upgrade, that wait never ends. Slack relay and browser CDP already bound handshake waits at 30s.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep a private `buildMattermostWebSocketClientOptions` as the single production options surface (`handshakeTimeout: 30_000`).
- Default Mattermost `WebSocket` factory consumes that builder.
- Regressions observe that production wiring in source (knip-safe; no new unused exports) and prove stalled-handshake timeout returns control to `runWithReconnect`.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A Mattermost host that accepted TCP without completing the websocket handshake could pin the channel reconnect loop forever on that attempt.

target.title: fix: resolve Tavily SecretRefs in agent tools
target.body:
Fixes #95109

## Summary

- Select the active resolved runtime config snapshot in one shared helper before agent/plugin tool surfaces read credentials.
- Apply Tool Search defaults on top of that selected runtime config, so run-local overlays do not turn a resolved snapshot back into authored SecretRefs.
- Reuse the same selector from direct plugin-tool resolution and Tool Search resolution, avoiding drift between agent-visible plugin tools and direct plugin tools.
- Update Tavily's plugin-local API-key resolver to use inspect-mode SecretRef handling so a matching unresolved `env:*:TAVILY_API_KEY` ref can use the documented `process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY` fallback.
- Keep explicit non-env and nonmatching Tavily SecretRefs fail-closed instead of silently replacing file, exec, or other env refs with the ambient Tavily key.
- Add focused regressions for the agent Tool Search runtime snapshot path and the Tavily env fallback credential boundary.

## Root Cause

There were two related Tavily SecretRef failures at different ownership layers.

1. The agent Tool Search runtime-config overlay selected the wrong base config. The embedded attempt path and harness bridge applied local Tool Search defaults directly to `params.config`. When `params.config` was the authored source config, the overlay clone no longer matched the active runtime source snapshot, so later plugin-tool config selection treated it as explicit config and did not swap in the already-resolved runtime snapshot. Tavily then received an exec-backed SecretRef instead of the resolved in-memory string.
2. Tavily's plugin-local resolver used strict SecretRef normalization before the documented env fallback. `extensions/tavily/src/config.ts` called strict normalization on `plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey`; an unresolved env SecretRef threw before `process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY` could be read.

RCA proof:

- Agent Tool Search before behavior: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts` and `src/agents/harness/tool-surface-bridge.ts` applied Tool Search defaults before runtime snapshot selection.
- Existing selector proof: direct plugin tools already used the source/runtime snapshot matching rule; this PR moves that rule into `src/agents/tool-runtime-config.ts` and reuses it.
- Tavily before behavior: `extensions/tavily/src/config.ts` used strict SecretRef normalization ahead of the env fallback, which matches the `UnresolvedSecretInputError` in #95109.
- Dependency contract inspected: `resolveSecretInputString` strict mode throws on unresolved refs; inspect mode returns ref metadata so the plugin can allow only the matching env fallback and block file/exec/wrong-env refs.

## What Problem This Solves

Users with Tavily configured through resolved runtime SecretRefs can use agent-visible Tavily tools without the Tool Search overlay reintroducing unresolved source SecretRefs.

Users with Tavily configured as `{ source: "env", provider: "default", id: "TAVILY_API_KEY" }` can also rely on the documented gateway environment fallback when that env ref is not inline-resolved in the current read-only plugin path. Tavily still does not silently borrow `TAVILY_API_KEY` for file refs, exec refs, or env refs targeting another variable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The agent runtime now chooses the applicable resolved runtime snapshot before applying local Tool Search defaults. That keeps run-local config overlays in memory, preserves the authored SecretRef in source config, and avoids storing plaintext credentials.

The Tavily plugin now mirrors the inspect-mode SecretRef pattern used by sibling web providers: it classifies configured secrets as available, missing, or blocked before deciding whether the ambient env fallback is allowed.

## User Impact

Agent-visible Tavily tools can use exec/file/env SecretRefs that have already been resolved into the active runtime snapshot.

Tavily also no longer throws before checking `TAVILY_API_KEY` for the canonical env SecretRef configuration reported in #95109. Explicit non-env Tavily SecretRefs remain fail-closed if unavailable.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior fixed: Tool Search runtime config now carries resolved in-memory Tavily API key values to agent/plugin tools while the source config keeps the authored SecretRef; Tavily's plugin-local resolver now allows the matching env SecretRef fallback without weakening file/exec/wrong-env credential boundaries.

Closest feasible environment tested: focused Vitest coverage through the actual agent Tool Search runtime helpers and Tavily resolver code, plus current-head terminal proof through the real `tavily_search` tool entrypoint. The current-head proof configured Tavily with an env SecretRef, set only a generated dummy `TAVILY_API_KEY`, and called the real Tavily endpoint. Tavily returned the expected dummy-key auth failure instead of OpenClaw throwing `UnresolvedSecretInputError`.

## What Problem This Solves

Managed Claude ACP sessions can fail before producing a response when OpenClaw forwards a disabled generic thinking value as a Claude `effort` config option. The installed Claude ACP adapter accepts `default`, `low`, `medium`, and `high`; values such as `off` and `none` are rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The failure belongs at the ACPX compatibility boundary: OpenClaw has valid cross-provider semantics for disabling thinking, while Claude ACP represents that state as `effort: default`.

This patch translates only disabled effort values for recognised Claude ACP effort/thinking aliases to the canonical `effort: default` reset. It preserves supported effort values, existing Claude model normalisation, and all non-Claude behaviour.

## User Impact

Managed Claude ACP sessions no longer fail with `Invalid value for config option effort: none` or `off` when thinking is disabled or inherited as disabled. Disabling effort also clears a previously applied explicit effort on persistent sessions instead of leaving it active.

target.title: fix(irc): disconnect on oversized inbound lines
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a broken or hostile IRC server could keep sending an unterminated line and make OpenClaw retain the growing input indefinitely while the channel remained connected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The IRC client now applies the protocol's existing 512-byte wire limit to both complete inbound lines and the pending unterminated record. The check reserves the terminating CRLF and measures UTF-8 bytes, then reports the protocol error and closes the socket before parsing oversized input.

## User Impact

IRC connections no longer grow memory without bound on oversized inbound records. Legal 512-byte lines, split socket writes, PING/PONG handling, and multibyte UTF-8 input within the limit continue to work.

## Evidence

- Real Linux TCP loopback server/client regression: a post-registration 1 MiB fragment without CRLF produced exactly `IRC inbound line exceeds the 512-byte limit`, closed the socket, and made the client not ready.
- Real TCP boundary control: a legal 510-byte PING payload split across two socket writes (512 bytes including CRLF) was delivered and received a PONG while the client remained ready.
- UTF-8 control: an oversized multibyte line was rejected by byte length rather than JavaScript character count.

target.title: feat(agents): add iteration budget for agent loop safety
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has heuristic loop detection and whole-run timeouts, but no explicit per-agent hard budget for LLM tool-calling rounds. Production reports show that some agent/model/channel combinations can keep calling tools after useful results are available, duplicate visible messages, or continue consuming model calls after lifecycle bugs.

This PR adds an opt-in circuit breaker for those cases. It is intentionally disabled by default and configurable per agent so long-horizon agents can keep larger budgets while high-risk chat/tool agents can be bounded.

Addresses: #6890, #75468, #89090, #79301, #75355, #77625, #74859, #82518

## Why This Change Was Made

The implementation adds:

- `agents.defaults.iterationBudget` and per-agent `agents.list[].iterationBudget` overrides.
- `enabled`, `maxIterations`, `subagentMaxIterations`, and `forceSummaryOnExhaustion` config fields.
- An `onBeforeToolCallingRound` agent-core hook that runs after a model emits tool calls but before those tools execute.
- Embedded-runner budget exhaustion handling that returns `budget_exhausted`.
- Harness opt-in via `supportsIterationBudget`, with built-in OpenClaw and Codex support.
- Fail-closed behavior when a selected harness does not support budget enforcement.

## User Impact

Default behavior is unchanged because the budget is disabled unless configured. When enabled, the budget caps LLM tool-calling rounds, not individual tool calls and not total long-horizon task duration. A single model response containing multiple tool calls counts as one round.

Operators can use this as a safety net for agents where runaway tool loops are more harmful than stopping early. Long-horizon agents should either leave the budget disabled or set an intentionally higher per-agent limit.

}

target.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Codex app-server over `websocket`/`unix` transport would hang forever on `initialize`/RPC when a peer accepted TCP but never completed the WebSocket upgrade. Pending frames never flush and the client never sees a transport exit, so the run cannot fail closed or reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add a private `buildCodexAppServerWebSocketOptions` that sets `handshakeTimeout: 30_000` (same floor as Slack relay / Mattermost / Discord gateway).
- Both TCP and Unix upgrade paths consume that builder.
- Guard `EventEmitter` error re-emit with `listenerCount` so callers that only wait on `exit` (handshake hang paths) are not disrupted by Node's unhandled-`error` throw.
- Add `testHooks` for test-only short handshake floors; production omits them and uses the 30s default.

Collision check: searched open PRs for "codex websocket handshake timeout app-server"; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

- **Before**: A peer that accepts TCP but never completes the WS upgrade hangs `CodexAppServerClient.initialize()` and all subsequent RPC calls forever — no timeout, no error, no reconnect.
- **After**: Handshake times out after 30s with a `close` event and error, allowing the client to fail closed or retry. Working WebSocket connections are unaffected.

## Verification

- Exact head: `6c71011`
- `oxfmt --check extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts proof-codex-ws-handshake.mts` — passed.
- `oxlint <same files>` — passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check` — passed; exit 0.
- Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```

 ✓ can speak JSON-RPC over the canonical unix control socket 14ms
 ✓ uses a 30s handshakeTimeout matching Slack relay / Mattermost 3ms
 ✓ negative control: ws without handshakeTimeout stays CONNECTING on never-upgrade peer 307ms
 ✓ emits exit when the websocket handshake never completes 205ms
 ✓ fails initialize when the websocket handshake never completes 206ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

- Standalone production-path proof (9 structured assertions):

```bash
node --import tsx proof-codex-ws-handshake.mts
```

```
node=v22.22.0
head=6c710118d0c766c98543928c8fd20b21061f7d51
[case 1] negative control — ws without handshakeTimeout stays CONNECTING
  ok: without handshakeTimeout, stays CONNECTING after 300ms
  ok: readyState is CONNECTING
  info: outcome=still-pending readyState=CONNECTING wait_ms=300

[case 2] positive control — createWebSocketTransport times out
  ok: production handshake timeout is 30s
  ok: transport killed after timeout
  ok: exit code is 1006 (abnormal closure)
  ok: resolved in under 2s (not 30s production floor)
  ok: resolved after the proof timeout
  info: killed=true exit_code=1006 elapsed_ms=201 proof_timeout_ms=200 production_timeout_ms=30000

[case 3] valid server — client communicates over real WebSocket
  ok: RPC responded with expected result
  ok: resolved in under 1s
  info: elapsed_ms=14

=== Summary ===
production_timeout_ms: 30000
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 9 passed, 0 failed
```

- Mutation check: temporarily revert `buildCodexAppServerWebSocketOptions` to omit `handshakeTimeout` → case 2 hangs (no `exit` event within 5s) → restore → passes.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** WebSocket handshake timeout on stalled peer through production entry points `createWebSocketTransport` + `CodexAppServerClient` (not raw `ws` library).
- **Real environment tested:** Node 22, real `ws` library, local loopback TCP server (accepts but never sends WS upgrade response), real `WebSocketServer` for valid-response roundtrip.
- **Exact commands run:**

```bash
node --import tsx proof-codex-ws-handshake.mts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 9 passed, 0 failed (exit 0)
```

- **Observed result after fix:**
  - **Negative control** (case 1): Raw `ws` without `handshakeTimeout` stays `CONNECTING` on never-upgrade TCP peer — confirmed `still_pending` after 300ms, proves the pre-fix hang.
  - **Positive control** (case 2): `createWebSocketTransport` with `handshakeTimeoutMs: 200` exits with code `1006` after `201ms` — production timeout bounds the handshake at the `ws` library level, the caller gets a transport exit.
  - **Valid response** (case 3): `createWebSocketTransport` + `CodexAppServerClient.fromTransportForTests` completes a JSON-RPC roundtrip over a real `WebSocketServer` in `~14ms` — fix does not affect working connections.
  - **Production constant** is `30_000ms` (same floor as Slack relay / Mattermost / Discord gateway).
  - **Vitest regression tests**: 6 passed, including negative control (CONNECTING hang) and initialize-timeout proof.

- **What was not tested:** Real Codex app-server with live Codex CLI; real Unix socket transport (tested via vitest mocks). The fix operates at the `ws` library `WebSocket.ClientOptions.handshakeTimeout` level — the standalone proof tests that boundary through the production `createWebSocketTransport` function with a real TCP server and real `ws` negotiation.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** the proof uses a short `testHooks.handshakeTimeoutMs: 200` to avoid wall-clock 30s waits; the production constant is verified via a separate assertion (`HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS === 30_000`). The hung peer intentionally accepts TCP and never completes the WS upgrade to simulate a broken/evil peer scenario.

## Risk / Compatibility

target.title: fix(discord): keep voice participant labels UTF-16 safe [AI-assisted]
target.body:
> [AI-assisted] This PR was generated using Claude Code.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord voice participant labels (nick / global name / username) could end up with a dangling UTF-16 surrogate half when the label is longer than 100 code units and an emoji lands on the truncation boundary.

`normalizeLabel` in `extensions/discord/src/voice/participant-context.ts` (introduced in #107004) truncated with a plain `normalized.slice(0, 100)`. Discord nicks and global names regularly contain emoji. When an emoji's surrogate pair straddles the 100-code-unit boundary, `slice(0, 100)` keeps the high surrogate and drops the low one, leaving a dangling `\uD83D`-style half that renders as `�` and can corrupt downstream JSON serialization / logs that consume the formatted participant line.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix swaps the bare `slice(0, 100)` for the shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper (from `@openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`), which is already used across the Discord extension (`error-body.ts`, `monitor/gateway-plugin.ts`, `monitor/message-handler.context.ts`, etc.) and across ~300 call sites repo-wide for exactly this class of truncation. Same pattern as #102246 (mushuiyu886, merged) and dozens of zhangguiping-xydt / mushuiyu886 UTF-16 safe truncation PRs.

The change is one import + one call-site replacement in `participant-context.ts`; no behavior change for labels that fit or that don't land an emoji on the boundary.

## User Impact

Voice participant lines (`- user_id=... display_name=...`) rendered to the agent / logs no longer carry a `�` or a dangling surrogate when a long Discord nick/global name is truncated mid-emoji. Labels <= 100 code units are unchanged.

## Evidence

Real behavior captured by driving the real exported `formatDiscordVoiceParticipantStateLine` with a participant whose nick is `"m".repeat(99) + "😀"` (101 UTF-16 code units - the emoji's surrogate pair straddles the 100 boundary).

**Before fix (current `main`)** - `slice(0, 100)` splits the `😀` surrogate pair, leaving a dangling high surrogate:

```
nick_length: 101
label_length: 100
has_dangling_surrogate: true
label_preview: "mmmm\ud83d"
```

**After fix** - `truncateUtf16Safe` backs the boundary off the surrogate pair:

```
nick_length: 101
label_length: 99
has_dangling_surrogate: false
label_preview: "mmmmm"
```

Regression test in `extensions/discord/src/voice/participant-context.test.ts` (`keeps participant labels UTF-16 safe when an emoji lands on the truncate boundary`): failing-first, asserts the parsed `display_name` label has no dangling surrogate and stays within 100 code units.

Local verification:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/voice/participant-context.test.ts` - 2/2 pass (failing-first on `main`).
- `oxlint` + `oxfmt --check` on changed files - pass.

Not tested: live Discord voice state events (the proof drives the real `formatDiscordVoiceParticipantStateLine` formatter directly with a participant state shaped like a real `APIVoiceState.member.nick`).

target.title: PR5/5 durable core: internal session delivery handoff
target.body:
## Upstream cumulative PR / focused review target

This PR is opened directly against `openclaw/openclaw:release/2026.7.1` because GitHub cannot target an upstream PR at another fork PR branch. It is therefore cumulative in the GitHub "Files changed" view.

**Focused review target:** please review the immediate predecessor diff `ea4627cfeaf507bee5d6c3b3f18419e669fcb60a..be7e16817cd71fef0bbecdc6c847aecdad971c6b` (PR4′ (this stack immediate predecessor) → PR5′ head). The cumulative ancestry is intentional and verified.


@clawsweeper review

Historical reviewed predecessor: old upstream #106443 covered the earlier version of this slice. It is useful review context only; please review this current upstream PR/head/base package fresh.

# PR5/5 - internal session delivery handoff + final hardening

## What Problem This Solves

This finishes the clean upstream durable-core stack by turning resolved durable wake
obligations into an internal session delivery-queue handoff on gateway startup.
After PR4 made wakes inspectable and controllable, PR5 gives the durable runtime
a concrete recovery path: a resolved wake is replayed, persisted with delivery
evidence, and queued for the owning OpenClaw session without inventing external
channel sends.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR5/5
- PR: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106443
- Clean PR5 comparison: `a30e2b6ce4e5f1390599380aedc82078c98854f7..443ffd2292e146fad3c089a03382a5f4702632f7`
- PR4 dependency: `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105844`
- GitHub base rationale: existing PR1-PR4 stack PRs target `release/2026.7.1`; the PR4 branch exists on the fork, not as an upstream base branch, so this PR follows stack convention while documenting the exact PR4-head diff.

## Scope

- Adds `createDurableWakeSessionDeliveryHook`, which resolves durable wakes to
  agent/session keys and enqueues one internal `systemEvent` via the session
  delivery queue.
- Wires gateway startup durable wake replay through that hook.
- Persists delivery evidence with `internalDelivery: "session_delivery_queue"`
  and `noExternalSend: true`.
- Extends focused replay/startup tests for idempotency, startup replay, ambiguous
  target handling, and no autonomous resume/abandon/create-new policy.
- Updates durable docs to clarify the `delivered` state and CLI wake-attempt
  evidence.

## Non-scope

- No Discord, Signal, Slack, plugin, or other external transport delivery is
  implemented or claimed.
- No cron mutation.
- No release/changelog/package churn from the stale old PR5 ancestry.
- No broad durable orchestration policy changes beyond this internal handoff.

## Evidence

Clean scope:

```text
6 files changed, 372 insertions(+), 50 deletions(-)
```

Focused behavior:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/durable/wake-delivery-replay.test.ts src/durable/startup.test.ts
# pass: 2 files, 14 tests
```

Adjacent durable CLI/Gateway/read-path proof:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/durable.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/durable.test.ts src/durable/wake-controls-inspection.test.ts
# pass: 3 Vitest shards, 4 files, 25 tests
```

Static/docs gates:

```bash
pnpm check:test-types
# pass

pnpm check:docs
# pass

git diff --check a30e2b6ce4e5f1390599380aedc82078c98854f7..HEAD
# pass
```

Remote proof attempts were made but unavailable in this shell:

```text
blacksmith-testbox: blocked, blacksmith CLI not found in PATH
aws Crabbox: blocked, broker login missing
```

## Upgrade contract

This PR adds no schema migration. It writes wake delivery attempts using the
existing durable wake attempt ledger and queues internal session deliveries using
the existing session delivery queue idempotency contract. Repeated startup replay
must not duplicate queued events once a wake is marked delivered.

## Risk / limits

- Main risk is semantic: reviewers should confirm `delivered` remains scoped to
  internal durable/session handoff and cannot be mistaken for external channel
  transport success.
- Remote Testbox proof is still desirable before merge because local provider
  setup blocked it here.
- Full release validation was not run for this narrow PR5 slice.

@clawsweeper review

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.20.6 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 1 July 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.16, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3956

4.37.0 - 08 Jul 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.0. #3995
  • In addition to the existing input format, the config-file input for the codeql-action/init step will soon support a new [owner/]repo[@ref][:path] format. All components except the repository name are optional. If omitted, owner defaults to the same owner as the repository the analysis is running for, ref to main, and path to .github/codeql-action.yaml. Support for this format ships in this version of the CodeQL Action, but will only be enabled over the coming weeks. #3973

4.36.3 - 01 Jul 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.2 - 04 Jun 2026

  • Cache CodeQL CLI version information across Actions steps. #3943
  • Reduce requests while waiting for analysis processing by using exponential backoff when polling SARIF processing status. #3937
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.6. #3948

4.36.1 - 02 Jun 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.0 - 22 May 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.19.4. #3894
  • Add support for SHA-256 Git object IDs. #3893
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.5. #3926

4.35.5 - 15 May 2026

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791
  • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

4.35.4 - 07 May 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881

4.35.3 - 01 May 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.19.3 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 9 April 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.15, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3837
  • Configurations for private registries that use Cloudsmith or GCP OIDC are now accepted. #3850
  • Best-effort connection tests for private registries now use GET requests instead of HEAD for better compatibility with various registry implementations. For NuGet feeds, the test is now always performed against the service index. #3853
  • Fixed a bug where two diagnostics produced within the same millisecond could overwrite each other on disk, causing one of them to be lost. #3852

target.title: fix(text): strip MiniMax marker from channel replies

Closes #105113

## What Problem This Solves

Official MiniMax Anthropic-compatible streams can append `[e~[` at the end of an assistant message. The earlier shared text sanitizer was too broad: it receives text without provider or transport identity, so it could remove ordinary prose from unrelated hosted MiniMax routes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cleanup now belongs to `extensions/minimax` and is attached only to the `minimax` and `minimax-portal` provider hooks. ## User Impact

Official MiniMax and MiniMax Portal streams no longer expose the terminal marker. Literal marker-like prose, tool-use turns, and interleaved reasoning/text blocks remain intact. Ollama Cloud MiniMax routes are unchanged for both native and OpenAI-compatible transports.

target.title: fix(memory): bound unsignaled remote HTTP with default timeoutMs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory remote HTTP (`withRemoteHttpResponse`) only forwarded an optional caller `AbortSignal`. Embedding batch / `postJson` callers often omit a signal (Google/OpenAI/Voyage upload and status polls), so a peer that accepts TCP but never returns headers could hang the Gateway forever. Idle body caps never start until headers arrive. Callers that pass a cancellation-only `AbortSignal` (no deadline) had the same hang risk when the wrapper treated any signal as a reason to skip the transport floor.

## Why This Change Was Made

Install a shared hang floor via existing `fetchWithSsrFGuard` `timeoutMs`, and compose it with any caller `AbortSignal`:

- Default: `MEMORY_REMOTE_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` = 120s (aligned with memory remote batch budgets so large uploads are not clamped below established policy)
- Explicit `timeoutMs` override still wins
- Caller `AbortSignal` is always forwarded; `fetchWithSsrFGuard` / `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` compose cancellation with the floor so cancellation-only signals cannot disable the hang bound

Also forward optional `timeoutMs` through `postJson` so production JSON POST callers can override the floor without reimplementing the wrapper.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** Unsignaled (or cancellation-only-signaled) memory remote HTTP could hang indefinitely on a stalled upstream.

**After:** Requests fail closed after 120s by default (`TimeoutError` / `request timed out`), including when a caller supplies a cancellation-only `AbortSignal`. Explicit `timeoutMs` and earlier caller aborts still win.

## Evidence

- Changed: `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/remote-http.ts`, `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/post-json.ts`
- Production path under test: `withRemoteHttpResponse` (shared by `postJson` / batch-upload / provider embedding batches) against a real local `node:http` server that never writes headers

target.title: refactor(cli): add p-map concurrency limit to capability CLI file operations
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `capability-cli.ts` uses `Promise.all` in 5 file-operation functions (`writeOutputAsset`, `readModelRunImageFiles`, `runImageGenerate`, `runImageDescribe`, `runVideoGenerate`), each spawning unbounded concurrent I/O or subprocess operations. On large batches (100+ files), this causes simultaneous file reads, image conversions, downloads, and inference requests at once - risking EMFILE exhaustion, OOM from buffering many image buffers simultaneously, connection-pool starvation for provider API calls, and CPU overcommit from parallel sharp image processing.

**Solution**: Replace 5 `Promise.all(x.map(async ...))` calls with `pMap(x, ..., { concurrency: 20 })`. p-map v7.0.5 is already a direct dependency used across 7+ other modules in the codebase including media-understanding, cron, and gateway server startup. No new dependencies introduced.

**What changed**: 5 async mapping locations in `src/cli/capability-cli.ts`. Each function's core logic and error handling remain unchanged - only the outer iteration over the dynamic array is bounded. The inner `Promise.all` calls within each iteration (e.g., per-image metadata gathering) continue to run in parallel as a fixed-size batch within one pMap slot.

**What did NOT change**: Inner per-item `Promise.all` calls, error handling, return types, function signatures, behavior for single or small-batch invocations. Zero behavioral change at the small scale covered by existing unit tests.

## Real behavior proof

**Environment**: Node.js v25.9.0, Linux x64, p-map v7.0.3, Minimax API (api.minimaxi.com, model MiniMax-M3).

**Test**: 20 concurrent inference requests sent to Minimax API via pMap with `{concurrency: 20}` - the identical library and parameter used in this PR. Each request is a real HTTPS call to a production AI provider.

target.title: fix(slack): pass upload timeoutMs through guarded fetch dispatcher floors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack outbound file upload already built a 120s `AbortSignal` via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, but `fetchWithSsrFGuard` did not receive `timeoutMs`. Guarded Undici dispatchers only apply connect/headers floors when `timeoutMs` is set; with signal alone, a peer that accepts TCP and never returns headers can hang until OS timeouts instead of failing on the shared transport floor. Sibling Feishu streaming-card / memory remote HTTP already pass both.

Open [#105893](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105893) only times out startup `auth.test`; it does not touch upload.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the existing upload budget into the guarded fetch:

```ts
timeoutMs: SLACK_UPLOAD_POST_TIMEOUT_MS,
```

No new config/env surface. AbortSignal composition and completion-dispatch safety comments stay unchanged.

## User Impact

**Before:** A hung Slack upload peer could stall the byte-upload path beyond the intended 120s transport floor when only AbortSignal was wired.

**After:** Upload uses the same 120s budget for both AbortSignal and Undici connect/headers floors, so accept-then-hang peers fail closed via the guarded dispatcher.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/slack/src/client-delivery.ts`
- Production caller: `sendMessageSlack` file upload → `fetchWithSsrFGuard`
- Sibling: Feishu streaming-card / memory remote HTTP `timeoutMs` + signal
- Regression: `extensions/slack/src/send.upload.test.ts`

### Caller-path Vitest

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/send.upload.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ ... > uploads bytes to the presigned URL and completes with thread+caption
 ✓ ... > times out a hanging presigned URL upload
 ✓ ... > fails closed on a hung upload peer via guarded timeoutMs floor 89ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  35 passed (35)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 4.93s
```

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:**
Slack upload omitted `timeoutMs` on `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, so Undici connect/headers floors were not applied despite a 120s AbortSignal.

**Canonical reachability path:**
`sendMessageSlack` → `client-delivery` upload POST → `fetchWithSsrFGuard(withTrustedEnvProxyGuardedFetchMode(...))`

**Shared helper / provider constraint check:**
`fetchWithSsrFGuard` only passes dispatcher timeout when `params.timeoutMs` is set (`resolveDispatcherTimeoutMs`).

**Real environment tested:**
Local Vitest against a real loopback `node:http` server that accepts the upload request and never writes headers.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/send.upload.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ ... > fails closed on a hung upload peer via guarded timeoutMs floor 89ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 4.93s
```

**Observed result after fix:**
Production path passes `timeoutMs: 120_000`. Against a hung peer, the guarded dispatcher fails closed in ~80ms when the proof substitutes that short stand-in (production floor remains 120s).

**What was not tested:**
Live Slack files API credentials; full 120s production floor duration.

target.title: fix(qqbot): bound gateway websocket handshake waits at 30s
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QQBot gateway websocket creation set headers/proxy agent but not `handshakeTimeout`. `gateway-connection` sets `isConnecting=true` until `open` or `close`; when a peer accepts TCP but never completes the websocket upgrade, that flag stays true forever and reconnect is skipped (`Already connecting, skip`). Slack relay, Mattermost, and Signal already bound handshake waits at 30s.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Bake `handshakeTimeout: 30_000` into `createQQWSClient` via `QQBOT_WEBSOCKET_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS`.
- Timeout-induced `close` already clears `isConnecting` and drives `scheduleReconnect` — no gateway-connection logic change.
- Regressions assert constructor wiring and prove a real TCP hang fails at ~30s.

No new config/env surface.

Note: open [#99075](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99075) bounds `maxPayload` in the same factory; this PR only adds handshake timeout and should rebase cleanly after that lands.

## User Impact

**Before:** A QQBot gateway peer that accepted TCP without completing the websocket handshake could pin the channel in a permanent connecting state with no reconnect.

**After:** Handshake waits fail closed after 30s (`Opening handshake has timed out` / close 1006), clearing `isConnecting` so reconnect continues.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/ws-client.ts`
- Production caller: `gateway-connection.ts` → `createQQWSClient`
- Sibling: Slack relay / Mattermost / Signal `handshakeTimeout: 30_000`

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw cron run` (a manual/operator run) on a `deleteAfterRun` one-shot ("at") job used to delete the job on success — consuming the one-shot so its scheduled fire never happened (issue #83538). Manual runs also mutated `consecutiveErrors` / `consecutiveSkipped` counters and `nextRunAtMs`, corrupting the scheduled retry/backoff/next-run state that only real scheduler executions should own.

The root cause is that `applyJobResult()` had no notion of *who* triggered a run: manual, scheduled (timer), and the gateway on-exit watcher all shared one finalization path, so `shouldDelete` and the counter mutations fired for every successful run regardless of origin.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix threads an explicit `CronRunOrigin` (`"timer" | "watcher-terminal" | "operator"`) through cron finalization. `applyJobResult` derives `consumesOneShot` and `ownsSchedulerState` as `origin !== "operator"` and records `lastRunWasManual = origin === "operator"`, so operator runs record the outcome only (never consume a `deleteAfterRun` one-shot, never touch scheduler counters / `nextRunAtMs` / enabled state), while `timer` and `watcher-terminal` runs keep consuming and owning scheduler state — preserving the merged on-exit `deleteAfterRun` contract from #104550.

`origin` is kept strictly internal. It is **not** part of the public `CronServiceRunOptions`: exposing it there would let any in-process facade caller (plugin SDK, RPC handlers, tests) request `watcher-terminal` semantics and delete one-shots or mutate scheduler-owned counters/backoff/timing. Instead, the public `run` is always operator semantics, and the gateway on-exit watcher — the only legitimate non-operator caller, which already holds the concrete `CronService` instance — uses a concrete-only `CronService.runOnExitTerminal` entry (absent from `CronServiceContract` / `GatewayCronServiceContract`) to get consuming behavior. The invalid-persisted-run path (`skipInvalidPersistedManualRun`) also forwards the true caller origin instead of hard-coding `operator`, so an invalid watcher-terminal run keeps scheduler-owned semantics.

## User Impact

- Debugging/manually running a scheduled `deleteAfterRun` job no longer silently cancels its upcoming scheduled fire.
- Manual runs no longer corrupt retry backoff, auto-disable, or next-run timing of scheduled jobs.
- Gateway on-exit watcher-terminal one-shots continue to be consumed exactly as before (no regression for the #104550 contract).
- The scheduler-consuming origin is no longer reachable through the public cron API, so plugins/RPC/tests cannot accidentally (or intentionally) delete one-shots or mutate scheduler state via `run`.

## Evidence

Real-setup proof at the current head using a **real running OpenClaw gateway process and the real `openclaw cron` CLI** (not a vitest/function harness). Built from this head and run inside a `node:24-bookworm` container (container node v24.18.0; the repo engines floor is 24.15.0), against a real on-disk cron store (sqlite).

```
Head: c071ce7ca34e7a41e4fafab4a8863960fb9403c7
Gateway: OpenClaw 2026.7.2 (c071ce7)   dist/build-info.json commit = c071ce7c...

Built-artifact fix verification (fix compiled into the running gateway):
  dist/server-cron-*.js contains:
    async runOnExitTerminal(id, payload) { ... }
    run: (jobId, payload) => cron.runOnExitTerminal(jobId, payload)
  'watcher-terminal' occurs only inside runOnExitTerminal; the public run path
  forwards no origin.

PART A — OPERATOR PRESERVATION (real `openclaw cron run`)
  $ openclaw cron add "partA-ok-preserve" --at "+2h" --command "echo ..." --delete-after-run
    -> id 3c309f88..., nextRunAtMs 1784045230759
  $ openclaw cron run 3c309f88... --wait
    -> {"status":"ok", exitCode 0}          (operator path, success)
  $ openclaw cron get 3c309f88...
    -> job STILL PRESENT, enabled:true, deleteAfterRun:true,
       nextRunAtMs 1784045230759 (UNCHANGED), lastRunWasManual:true,
       no consecutiveErrors / no backoff mutation
  => successful operator run did NOT consume the one-shot, scheduler state intact.

PART B — WATCHER-TERMINAL CONSUMPTION (real gateway on-exit watcher cycle)
  $ openclaw cron add "partB-onexit-consume" --on-exit "sleep 8; echo ..." \
        --command "echo ..." --delete-after-run
  # real gateway watcher armed + spawned the watched process (seen in ps):
  #   bash -lc sleep 8   /   sleep 8
  [cron] cron-exit: watcher armed { jobId: a27c2044... }
  [cron] cron-exit: watched command exited; firing job { exitCode: 0 }
  $ openclaw cron get a27c2044...      -> "cron job not found"
  $ openclaw cron list                 -> only the 2 PART A jobs remain
  $ sqlite3 .../openclaw.sqlite 'select job_id from cron_jobs'  -> 2 rows (no partB)
  => real on-exit watcher-terminal run DID consume/delete the successful one-shot.

OVERALL: PASS — driven end-to-end through a live gateway + operator CLI + real
on-disk store. Operator and watcher-terminal origins are cleanly separated, and
the scheduler-consuming origin is unreachable from the public cron API.
```

Unit/regression coverage at head: the public `CronServiceContract.run` preserves a `deleteAfterRun` one-shot (operator semantics, no scheduler-state mutation) even though it can no longer request another origin, `CronService.runOnExitTerminal` still consumes a successful on-exit one-shot, and invalid watcher-terminal runs keep scheduler-owned semantics while operator invalid runs stay operator-attributed.

target.title: fix(plugins): restore nested registry state on failed registration rollback
target.body:
Fixes #106647

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a failed plugin registration could leave nested registry state partially applied. OpenClaw snapshots the plugin registry for transactional rollback, but the snapshot only copied top-level arrays and maps while keeping references to nested `PluginRecord` objects and existing capability entries. During registration, the loader mutates those objects in place (for example appending `toolNames` or extending middleware `runtimes`). On rollback, the array structure was restored while the mutated nested fields remained, so a failed plugin load could poison later retries and leave inconsistent registry metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

Registration rollback now isolates transaction-owned mutable state without cloning the entire registry with `structuredClone` (which would break function-bearing handlers). Array and record entries get property-level snapshots that clone mutable arrays/values while keeping handlers by reference. The live `PluginRecord` being registered is included even before it is pushed onto `registry.plugins`, and all loader registration transactions pass that record through. This keeps one canonical rollback path, preserves executable handlers, and restores counters/lists after failure.

Fix quality: compatibility — no config/API change, runtime-only isolation; performance — snapshot cost only at registration boundaries, not request hot paths; usability — failed loads no longer leave sticky partial metadata; security — no trust-boundary change, fail closed still rolls back side effects.

## User Impact

Operators and developers who hit a plugin registration failure during load, setup-runtime registration, or CLI metadata registration get a clean rollback of plugin records and nested capability entries. A retry after a failed registration starts from the pre-failure registry state instead of carrying over tool names, route counters, errors, or middleware runtime lists from the failed attempt.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS 15 (Node 24.17.0)

Transaction-boundary unit coverage:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/plugin-registration-transaction.test.ts
 ✓ |plugins| src/plugins/plugin-registration-transaction.test.ts (4 tests)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

Product-path load/retry coverage (deliberately broken plugin registration + clean retry via `loadOpenClawPlugins`):

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/loader.test.ts -t "restores nested registry metadata after failed load"
[proof] after failed registration {"failedStatus":"error","failedError":"Error: deliberate registration failure","failedToolNames":[],"tools":[],"middleware":[{"pluginId":"existing-stable","runtimes":["openclaw"]}]}
[proof] after clean retry {"cleanStatus":"loaded","cleanToolNames":["retry_target_tool"],"diagnostics":[],"tools":["retry_target_tool"],"middleware":[{"pluginId":"existing-stable","runtimes":["openclaw"]}]}
 ✓ |bundled| src/plugins/loader.test.ts (1 test)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 168 skipped (169)
```

Regression coverage:

1. Restoring the live current `PluginRecord` after failed registration (`toolNames`, `httpRoutes`, `hookCount`, `contextEngineIds`, `error`).
2. Restoring in-place mutations on existing middleware registrations (`runtimes`) while preserving handler function identity and required `source` metadata.
3. Product loader path: a deliberately broken plugin mutates nested middleware `runtimes` and `toolNames`, fails registration, leaves no sticky tools/middleware, preserves a sibling plugin's middleware `runtimes: ["openclaw"]`, then a fixed entry path for the same plugin id loads cleanly with `retry_target_tool`.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Failed plugin registration through the real `loadOpenClawPlugins` path no longer leaves sticky nested registry metadata; a subsequent clean load of the same plugin id succeeds without carrying failed-attempt tools or middleware runtimes.
- Environment: local macOS 15, OpenClaw checkout at this PR head, Node 24.17.0 via repo Vitest plugins/bundled config.
- Current-main contrast: On main, shallow registry snapshots keep nested object identity, so in-transaction mutations of `PluginRecord.toolNames` or middleware `runtimes` can survive rollback. This PR property-level isolates mutable values for the current record and registry entries.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/loader.test.ts -t "restores nested registry metadata after failed load"
  ```
- Setup used:
  1. Load sibling plugin `existing-stable` with agent tool-result middleware `runtimes: ["openclaw"]`.
  2. Load deliberately broken plugin `retry-target` that registers middleware (then mutates nested `runtimes` with a second registration), registers tool `retry_target_tool`, then throws `deliberate registration failure`.
  3. Inspect registry after failure.
  4. Retry with a fixed entry path for the same plugin id that only registers the tool successfully.
- Evidence after fix (redacted runtime dumps from the command above):
  - After failed registration: `failedStatus=error`, `failedToolNames=[]`, `tools=[]`, middleware only `existing-stable` with `runtimes:["openclaw"]` (no sticky `retry-target` middleware / no `codex` runtime leak).
  - After clean retry: `cleanStatus=loaded`, `cleanToolNames=["retry_target_tool"]`, `tools=["retry_target_tool"]`, sibling middleware still `runtimes:["openclaw"]`.
- Control check: transaction unit file still passes 4/4; handler identity preservation remains covered there.
- Observed result after fix: product-path failed registration rolls back nested mutable state; clean retry for the same plugin id succeeds without leftover metadata from the failed attempt.
- What was not tested: long-lived multi-plugin gateway process with a third-party npm package install/uninstall cycle outside the loader harness. The harness exercises the same `loadOpenClawPlugins` + `createPluginRegistrationTransaction` registration path used by gateway/CLI loads.

target.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention
target.body:
## Problem

The exec-approvals store uses two lock mechanisms sharing the same `.lock` file:

1. **Async sidecar lock** (via `@openclaw/fs-safe`): Used by `resolveExecApprovalsLocked`, `updateExecApprovals`, `loadExecApprovalsAsync`. Has `allowReentrant: true`.

2. **Sync custom lock** (`acquireExecApprovalsLockSync`): Used by `loadExecApprovals`, `readExecApprovalsSnapshot`, `resolveExecApprovals`.

When the async lock holds the `.lock` file (e.g., during `ensureExecApprovalsSnapshot`), the sync lock attempts fail immediately because `acquireExecApprovalsLockSync` detects `ownerPid === process.pid` and treats it as self-deadlock — it does not retry. The failure triggers `createFailClosedExecApprovalsFallback()` → `security: "deny"`. All subsequent execs see `security=deny` and are denied.

The key condition in `acquireExecApprovalsLockSync`:
```typescript
if (state.ownerPid !== null && state.ownerPid !== process.pid && attempt < RETRIES) {
    sleepExecApprovalsSyncLockRetry();
    continue;
}
throw error; // Falls through for same-PID → immediate fail
```

## Fix

Added `isExecApprovalsProcessLocalLockContention()` to detect this specific scenario: `file_lock_timeout` error where the lock is owned by the current process and the target file already exists.

Modified `withExecApprovalsReadLockSync()` to catch same-process contention in both code paths and fall back to lockless reads.

### Why this is safe

- Async writes use atomic temp-file + rename → concurrent reads always see a consistent snapshot
- Only applies to **read** locks — write serialization is preserved
- Lockless fallback only triggers when the **target file already exists**, preserving fail-closed behavior during initial policy creation (no file yet → writer must not be bypassed)

## Changes

- `src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`: Added `isExecApprovalsProcessLocalLockContention()` helper + modified `withExecApprovalsReadLockSync()` (both code paths)
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-store.test.ts`: Added test that simulates same-process lock contention and verifies `loadExecApprovals()` and `readExecApprovalsSnapshot()` return real policy instead of fail-closed deny

## Testing

All 72 exec-approvals store tests pass, including the new test and the existing "fails closed when a writer locks the store before creating the policy file" test (which verifies the fail-closed path is preserved when the target file doesn't exist).

Closes #106777

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Same-process sync/async lock contention in exec-approvals causes all exec commands to be denied with security=deny when the async sidecar lock is held during synchronous policy reads (issue #106777).

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node.js v24.16.0, OpenClaw gateway running locally with single-process mode.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```
cd /mnt/data/repos/forks/openclaw
npx vitest run src/infra/exec-approvals-store.test.ts --no-coverage
```

**Evidence after fix**:
```
RUN  v4.1.9 /mnt/data/repos/forks/openclaw

 ✓  infra  ../../src/infra/exec-approvals-store.test.ts (72 tests) 435ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  72 passed (72)
   Start at  20:21:35
   Duration  911ms (transform 332ms, setup 231ms, import 122ms, tests 435ms, environment 0ms)
```

**Observed result after fix**: All 72 tests pass including the new same-process lock contention test (verifies loadExecApprovals and readExecApprovalsSnapshot return real policy instead of fail-closed deny) and the existing fail-closed test (verifies deny when target file does not exist). The lockless read fallback correctly activates only for same-PID contention when the policy file already exists.

**What was not tested**: Multi-process lock contention across separate gateway instances (requires Docker or multi-node setup). Windows-specific file locking behavior. Production gateway with high-frequency concurrent exec calls.

target.title: fix(file-transfer): reject oversized dir.fetch preflights
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users pulling a directory through `dir.fetch` could pass the approval/preflight step even when the paired node already estimates the tree is larger than the configured `maxBytes` budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node-host `dir.fetch` preflight path now reuses the same existing directory size gate that the archive path uses before returning the entry list to the gateway approval flow. This keeps the fix inside the file-transfer node boundary and leaves config, policy, archive validation, and path authorization behavior unchanged.

## User Impact

Oversized directory pulls now fail during the preflight phase with the existing `TREE_TOO_LARGE` result instead of appearing approval-ready and only failing when the archive transfer is requested.

## Evidence
